notes.summary: A Cloze Test is a short passage with five blanks. For each blank you choose the best word from four options. Tier 1 always has one cloze passage (5 questions). Blanks test vocabulary, grammar (tense, prepositions, connectors) and the logic of the passage.

concepts.title: Read the whole passage first
concepts.body: Read the full passage once without filling anything. Understand the topic and tone (positive, critical, narrative). Many blanks are decided by a sentence that comes after the blank.

concepts.title: Grammar check, then meaning
concepts.body:
For each blank:
  1. What part of speech is needed? (noun, verb, adjective, connector)
  2. Does the verb agree with its subject and tense?
  3. Which remaining option fits the meaning and tone?

concepts.title: Connectors
concepts.body: but, however, although → contrast; and, also, moreover → addition; so, therefore, as a result → result; because, since → reason. Choosing the right connector depends on how the two ideas relate.

varieties.name: Vocabulary blanks
varieties.how: Use the passage's meaning and tone to choose between words of the same part of speech.

example.q: The festival was a great success; thousands of people ___ the stalls.
steps: Options: avoided / visited / closed / feared → visited.

varieties.name: Grammar and connector blanks
varieties.how: Check the subject–verb agreement, tense and the logical link between clauses.

example.q: She was tired, ___ she kept working.
steps: Options: so / because / but / and → but.

tips: Re-read the complete passage with all your answers filled in before moving on.
If an option makes the passage contradict itself, it is wrong even if it fits the single sentence.
traps: Options that fit the sentence alone but not the passage's overall tone.
Two near-synonyms where only one collocates with the next word (e.g. make vs do).

passages.title: Saving Water
passages.text: Water is one of our most precious resources, yet we often (1)___ it carelessly. A single dripping tap can (2)___ thousands of litres in a year. Simple habits, such as turning off the tap (3)___ we brush our teeth, can make a real difference. Farmers, too, are learning to use drip irrigation, which (4)___ water directly to the roots of plants instead of flooding whole fields. If each of us takes small steps today, the growing problem of water (5)___ can be greatly reduced.

passages.title: The Old Teacher
passages.text: Mr. Iyer had taught in the village school for thirty years. He was (1)___ for his patience; no matter how many times a child got a sum wrong, he would explain it again with a smile. When the school (2)___ a new computer room, many expected the old teacher to retire. Instead, he spent his evenings learning how to type and how to (3)___ the internet. Within a few months he was helping the younger teachers prepare their lessons. His students noticed that he was never (4)___ to admit that he did not know something. ‘Learning,’ he often told them, ‘is not a race (5)___ a journey.’

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank (1).
questions.solution: The word carelessly and the contrast word yet (after 'precious') require a neutral action done badly: use it carelessly. 'Save/protect/value carelessly' make no sense.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank (2).
questions.solution: A dripping tap loses water, so it can waste thousands of litres.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank (3).
questions.solution: A clause (we brush our teeth) follows, and the actions happen at the same time, so the conjunction while is needed. During is a preposition and needs a noun, not a clause.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank (4).
questions.solution: which refers to drip irrigation (singular), and the passage is in the simple present, so delivers.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank (5).
questions.solution: The passage is about wasting and saving water, and a 'growing problem' that saving reduces is a shortage: water scarcity. Abundance and surplus are not problems to be reduced.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank (1).
questions.solution: The fixed phrase is known for a quality. The next clause describes his patience, so he was known for it.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank (2).
questions.solution: The story is in the past and the school is the doer, so the active simple past opened is correct. 'was opened a new room' is ungrammatical.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank (3).
questions.solution: how to is followed by the base form of the verb: how to type and how to use the internet.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank (4).
questions.solution: The point is that admitting ignorance did not embarrass him: he was never ashamed to admit it. 'Never eager/happy/proud to admit' would give the opposite, negative picture, which does not fit the admiring tone.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank (5).
questions.solution: The pattern not X but Y sets up a correction: learning is not a race but a journey.

flashcards.back: Read the whole passage once before filling any blank.
